title: A Regime-Adaptive Deep Learning Framework for Intraday Market Direction Forecasting Using Option Chain Microstructure Signals
affiliations: GLA University, GLA University and GLA University

detail.title: A Regime-Adaptive Deep Learning Framework for Intraday Market Direction Forecasting Using Option Chain Microstructure Signals
detail.abstract: Standard price-sequence models for intraday equity index prediction are structurally blind to the institutional information embedded in the live options market, information that the microstructure literature shows precedes spot price movement. This article proposes and evaluates a hierarchical multi-module framework that fuses four independently operating components: a Hidden Markov Model for daily macro-regime classification, a dual-output Temporal Convolutional Network estimating market phase and breakout probability from 60minute price sequences, a gradient-boosted tree classifier trained on 70 option-chain microstructure features including implied volatility skew dynamics, open interest momentum, and dealer gamma and delta exposure at ten-second granularity, and a regime-adaptive risk controller scaling stop-loss and position size parameters as a function of daily regime state. Experiments on live trading sessions of index options data demonstrate a 15-minute direction accuracy of 57.0%, rising to 62.4% with unsupervised regime filtering. Module-level contributions are assessed using ablation study, where it is found that option chain microstructure always outperforms price return features in terms of feature importance assessment. Pathological issues associated with model collapse are identified via the forensic examination of the Temporal Convolutional Network architecture, and the issue is addressed. Conjunction gate of the integrated architecture delivers a simulated annualized Sharpe ratio of 1.71 with maximum drawdown reduced to 4.1% from 6.8%.

title: SICP-Mamba: Support-Information-Conditioned Progressive State-Space Modeling for Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
affiliations: Shandong Normal University and Shandong Normal University

detail.title: SICP-Mamba: Support-Information-Conditioned Progressive State-Space Modeling for Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
detail.abstract: Few-shot medical image segmentation aims to delineate target organs or lesions from query images using only a few annotated support samples, which is important for reducing annotation burden in biomedical image analysis. However, reliable segmentation under limited supervision remains challenging because medical images often exhibit complex anatomical structures, large inter-patient variations, low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, and substantial intra-class morphological differences. Existing methods usually establish support--query correlations through prototype matching, feature fusion, or cross-attention. These strategies may focus on local similarities or pairwise token relations, leading to high computational cost and insufficient preservation of support priors during deep interaction. To address these challenges, we propose SICP-Mamba, a support-information-conditioned progressive state-space framework for few-shot medical image segmentation. Rather than simply replacing existing interaction modules with Mamba blocks, SICP-Mamba models support--query interaction as progressive support-state propagation and support-conditioned query refinement. Specifically, Support-State Propagation Mamba (SSPM) recurrently propagates target-related support states to alleviate support-prior attenuation, while Support-Conditioned Query Mamba (SCQM) selectively injects propagated support states into query feature refinement to enhance target-aware representations. This design enables efficient long-range cross-image dependency modeling with linear complexity while preserving structural priors and enhancing query responses, helping handle ambiguous boundaries, background interference, and morphological variations. Experiments on ABD-MRI, ABD-CT, Card-MRI, and P-MRI datasets show that SICP-Mamba achieves accurate target localization, improved boundary delineation, favorable generalization across different anatomical structures and imaging modalities, and a competitive accuracy--efficiency trade-off.

title: Are women underrepresented speaking at Foot and Ankle Conferences in UK and Europe
affiliations: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Are women underrepresented speaking at Foot and Ankle Conferences in UK and Europe
detail.abstract: Abstract: Background: Representation of women in senior orthopaedic roles remains low as a percentage across Europe, especially when 55% of UK medical students graduating are female. Inviting women to speak at conferences broadens topic perspectives and provides role models to encourage entry into Orthopaedic Surgery. Methods: Gender of invited speakers and first authors was identified from the British (BOFAS) and European (EFAS) Foot and Ankle Societies Annual meetings, and their respective journals, The Foot (BOFAS) and the Journal of Foot and Ankle Surgery (JFAS), from 2012 to 2025. Year matched chi squared tests of independence (p=0.05) compared EFAS with JFAS, BOFAS with The Foot, and technical versus non technical presentations. Results: Female journal first authorship and BOFAS speaker representation both increased from 2012 to 2025. Across matched year comparisons, female representation was lower at EFAS than JFAS (11.9% (Std 5.7%) vs 15.2% (Std 13.9%); χ²(1) = 5.9, p=0.016), and at BOFAS than The Foot (10.7% (Std 8.3%) vs 22.5% (Std 10%); χ²(1) = 29.1, p<0.001). A similar gap was found between BOFAS abstract authors and The Foot authorship (11.6% (Std 5.5%) vs 22.5% (Std 10%); χ²(1)=37.4, p<0.001), but not between EFAS abstract authors and JFAS authorship (18.1% (Std 10.6%) vs 15.2% (Std 3.9%); χ²(1)=0.08, p=0.78). Women delivered proportionally more non technical talks at EFAS (women; 10.2% (Std 14.3) vs men; 2.2% (Std 3.0), χ²(1)=10.9, p<0.001), a difference not seen at BOFAS (women; 30.7% (Std 36.7) vs men; 20.8% (Std 10.5), χ²(1)= 2.0, p=0.16).Conclusions: Women remain underrepresented relative to their academic contributions at Foot and Ankle conferences in Europe and the UK. Further strategies are needed to increase female representation in academic foot and ankle surgery.

title: The FraNchEstYN framework for modelling crop yield losses due to fungal diseases
affiliations: Council for Agricultural Research and Economics and National Research Council Institute of Biometeorology

detail.title: The FraNchEstYN framework for modelling crop yield losses due to fungal diseases
detail.abstract: Predictive models linking fungal disease epidemics to crop growth remain scarce, despite substantial and unevenly distributed yield losses across world regions. Here, we present FraNchEstYN, a modular simulation framework designed to fill this gap. The framework couples a temperature- and moisture-driven pathogen suitability to a Susceptible-Exposed-Infected-Removed (SEIR) epidemiological core, translating disease severity into yield loss through four damage mechanisms: light stealing, assimilate sapping, senescence acceleration, and radiation use efficiency reduction. Crop simulations can be executed internally or by ingesting simulated trajectories from external crop models at run time. The framework further includes a fungicide efficacy module, automatic calibration, and an output layer with performance metrics and optionally LLM-driven decision-support. Parameterised for wheat and its major diseases, FraNchEstYN was evaluated through sensitivity analyses and four open-data case studies: yellow rust in Egypt, Septoria tritici blotch in Indiana and Ethiopia, and wheat blast in Brazil, consistently reproducing severity dynamics and yield effects across contrasting climates and management practices. FraNchEstYN is released as an open-source R package, providing an extensible tool for disease-aware crop yield simulation.

title: Auditing the Hidden Pitfalls of Foundation-Model-Assisted Annotation in Agricultural Vision: A Cross-Domain Stress Test on Bean Leaf Disease Detection
affiliations: Guilin Institute of Information Technology, Guilin University of Electronic Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Guilin Institute of Information Technology, Hainan University, Guilin University of Electronic Technology and Guilin Institute of Information Technology

detail.title: Auditing the Hidden Pitfalls of Foundation-Model-Assisted Annotation in Agricultural Vision: A Cross-Domain Stress Test on Bean Leaf Disease Detection
detail.abstract: Foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) are increasingly used to draft annotations in agricultural computer vision, yet leaky splits, misaligned class protocols, and undisclosed holdout overlap can produce misleadingly high in-domain scores. We propose an eight-step audit protocol and apply it retrospectively to bean rust and angular leaf spot detection. The audit voids a reported +3.9 percentage-point SAM "victory," a false independent holdout (300/300 MD5 overlap with test), and quantifies species pollution (2,366 images). After reconstruction (clean_split_v4) and a hash-independent third-party holdout (New Gold 350 primary; 402 robustness), locked evaluation shows in-domain mAP50 ≈ 0.76–0.79 but independent-holdout mAP50 ≈ 0.26 (−50 pp for YOLO-MSHF on Gold 350; −56 pp on Gold 402). A post-audit box-granularity cleanup (90 leaf-level boxes removed) raised holdout mAP50 only +2.2 pp; collapse remains −50 pp. Backbone generation swaps, NR module re-runs (all within run-to-run noise vs. baseline 0.264), SAM relabeling, and species cleaning do not restore holdout performance; mixing a small target-batch subset into training is the only remedy with consistent positive transfer (+1.4 to +4.2 pp). t-SNE shows substantial feature overlap yet detection collapse. Per-class analysis rejects a class-ratio artifact: angular leaf spot collapses more (−63.7 pp) than bean rust (−35.9 pp). Rigorous dataset auditing—not neck redesign—is the primary contribution.

title: Shadow Cost of Commuting: Metro Expansions and Asymmetric Caregiving Reallocation
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

detail.title: Shadow Cost of Commuting: Metro Expansions and Asymmetric Caregiving Reallocation
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how transit infrastructure reshapes intra household time allocation and intergenerational human capital formation. Exploiting the staggered rollout of Chinese rapid transit networks, I estimate robust difference in differences models to identify causal shifts in family behavior. I document a stark nighttime reallocation of child care from grandparents to parents. Improved commuting efficiency allows grandparents to provide daytime support and return to their own residences, decoupling intergenerational care from strict cohabitation. However, because spatial frictions decline while sticky gender norms persist, this evening caregiving void triggers a severely asymmetric response. Mothers absorb the newly internalized domestic burden, increasing their nighttime caregiving by 8.0 percentage points, whereas paternal involvement remains completely inelastic. Crucially, this heightened caregiving occurs without any reduction in maternal market working hours. Constrained by rigid formal labor markets, mothers face a corner solution where they finance intensified child rearing by depleting their physiological capital, resulting in a 7.5 percentage point increase in physical illness. Despite this severe maternal health tax, the structural reallocation generates distinct positive intra household externalities. Treated children exhibit significant reductions in illness alongside cumulative gains in motor skills and formal enrichment. Simultaneously, liberating grandmothers from evening child care duties relaxes a binding dual caregiving constraint, allowing time substitution toward spousal care that yields substantial health improvements for grandfathers.
